headline: High-risk default interaction: dbt-core can feed warehouse data into Open Interpreter, which has broad filesystem and shell access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core does not expose a shared interactive channel, but Open Interpreter can read files and clipboard by default, so a manual copy-paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions into its tool loop. The pathway is not automatic and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies dbt-generated text into Open Interpreter's prompt or clipboard
IF dbt output is written to a file that Open Interpreter later reads as instructions
mitigations: Keep dbt outputs in a separate review-only folder
Disable clipboard-based handoff during analysis
Use a strict prompt template that strips executable-looking text
Review any copied SQL or YAML before pasting
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress to model providers. If warehouse extracts, logs, or credentials land locally, Open Interpreter can access them and potentially transmit them through configured APIs. The pair creates a default leakage path through shared local files.
conditions: IF warehouse exports or credentials are stored on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is pointed at a directory containing dbt artifacts or secrets
IF model-provider calls are enabled for the session
mitigations: Store dbt artifacts outside Open Interpreter's working directory
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
Restrict Open Interpreter to a dedicated empty workspace
Disable network egress for the session
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse API, while Open Interpreter can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write the filesystem. Their overlapping write surfaces create a realistic conflict over shared project files and generated artifacts, and Open Interpreter's filesystem sharing via files makes concurrent edits unsafe by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF dbt generates artifacts while Open Interpreter edits or commits the same repo
IF multiple Open Interpreter instances share the same filesystem state
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Check in generated artifacts only after manual review
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core produces warehouse-facing outputs that Open Interpreter can treat as input for shell, file, or git actions. Because Open Interpreter can act on those outputs without a built-in verification layer, a mistaken dbt artifact can cascade into destructive local commands or bad commits. The interaction is dangerous in default workflows.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes dbt-generated SQL, manifests, or logs as authoritative
IF the operator allows Open Interpreter to execute follow-on shell or git actions
IF dbt output contains an incorrect model or path
mitigations: Require human review before any shell execution
Compare dbt outputs against expected schemas
Use dry-run mode for downstream actions
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only analysis first
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and sends requests to configured model providers. If regulated warehouse data or local regulated files are present, the pair can violate retention or residency expectations because Open Interpreter's default logging and egress controls are not documented as compliant here. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the warehouse or local filesystem
IF Open Interpreter forwards prompts or file contents to a third-party model provider
IF retention or residency rules require tighter controls than the default setup
mitigations: Exclude regulated datasets from the shared workspace
Confirm provider and region settings before use
Delete transient artifacts after each session
Keep secrets out of local files
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing and retention controls
